gallery.title: File:Istanbul Vefa Bozaci 4881.jpg
gallery.description:
From the Wikipedia article: In 1876, brothers Haci Ibrahim and Haci Sadik established a boza shop in the Istanbul district of Vefa, close to the then center of entertainment, Direklerarası. This boza, with its thick consistency and tart flavor, became famous throughout the city, and is the only boza shop dating from that period still in business today. The firm is now run by Haci Sadik and Haci Ibrahim's great-great-grandchildren. 
The vessel it's poured from is an intermediate one: it's "brewn" in much larger vessels behind the door that's open.

gallery.title: File:Istanbul Marble Tower 3145.jpg
gallery.description: One of some pictures of this tower that, according to a text provided, was once in the sea, but when the coastline was filled with soil, it was on land. On older pictures one can see cars speeding by on a side where there now are a relaxed park and pedestrian grounds. The coastal road is now more to the south. Nearby (and shown on some pictures) are the southernmost parts of the Theodosian Walls (a flag on their last bastion). The text just mentioned also indicates that claims that the tower is from the 8th-12th period it is more probably built when Sultan Beyazit I in the 14th century threatened the Byzantine capital.
